title: Thanthai Periyar Visits Malaya: Spreading Rationalism to Plantation Workers (1929)
summary: In December 1929, Periyar E. V. Ramasamy toured the rubber plantations of colonial Malaya, igniting an egalitarian cultural renaissance among indentured Tamil laborers.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 197: காந்தியின் நகைச்சுவைச் சூழலுக்கேற்ப மாறியது
full_text:
In December 1929, Periyar E. V. Ramasamy arrived by passenger steamer in Penang, embarking on an extensive tour across the rubber plantations and ports of British Malaya and Singapore.

Hundreds of thousands of indentured Tamil laborers lived in squalor on colonial estates, working under grueling conditions while maintaining rigid caste divisions and spending meager wages on arrack and expensive temple rituals.

Addressing mass rallies of plantation workers in Kuala Lumpur and Ipoh, Periyar spoke with fiery moral indignation:
"My hardworking brothers and sisters! You crossed the turbulent seas to this foreign land. It is your muscle and sweat that cleared these tropical jungles and made these rubber estates flourish with wealth!

Yet why do you still carry the poison of caste prejudice in your hearts? Does self-mortification and piercing your flesh with hooks feed your hungry children?
Stop squandering your earnings on liquor and superstition! Pool your resources, build modern schools, and educate your daughters! Shed your caste titles and unite as self-respecting human beings. The hands that labor are the hands that sustain civilization!"

Periyar's tour ignited a sweeping social reform movement across Southeast Asia, leading directly to the establishment of the Tamils Reform Association, community schools, and the social emancipation of plantation workers.
